verification.title: BREAKING: WWE And Montez Ford Hit With Lawsuit Over NSFW Approach With Counts Including Assault And Battery

text:
Following an incident on WWE RAW in July 2026, the company and Montez Ford have been hit with a lawsuit over an "unwanted sexualized" approach. 14 counts have been included in the lawsuit, including assault and battery.
Ad
Montez Ford and WWE are being sued
During an episode of WWERAW in July 2026, Montez Ford and Angelo Dawkins were making their way through the crowd. As part of the entrance, Ford approached the officer and did a dance around him while he looked bemused and remained stoic. The moment went viral as fans enjoyed it, and it was later posted on WWE social media as well.
Ad
MUST READS
The officer, Noel Lucas, has now filed a lawsuit against Ford, WWE, and Events LLC, accusing Ford of performing an unwanted sexualized "lap dance" on him during a live broadcast on Netflix, and WWE has since promoted the footage on social media as well. There were 14 counts, including assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, and violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act.
Expand Tweet
Ad
Post Wrestling reported that Lucas alleged Ford danced toward him without warning or consent, and after the video got hundreds of thousands of views on WWE and Ford's accounts, he became publicly recognized. At his full-time job at the courthouse the next day, "members of the public recognized him from the videos of the encounter that had circulated on social media and mocked him, thrusting their hips in his direction, imitating the sexual movements." He also said his children were mocked and ridiculed at school because of the video.
Ad
The lawsuit alleged the following:
“Defendant Crawford then began performing a sexually provocative dance immediately in front of and over Plaintiff, repeatedly thrusting and gyrating his hips and pelvis towards Plaintiff, performing a sexualized ‘lap dance.' [Crawford] moved his body increasingly closer to [Lucas]; continued the lap dance. [Crawford’s] left inner thigh repeatedly rubbed against Plaintiff’s leg."
Ad
Montez Ford's real name is Kenneth Crawford.
WWE has not issued a statement, but a hearing is set for December 10.
